subject: sociology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

options: Shared values and agreement that hold society together
questions.explain: Consensus approaches, like functionalism, stress that shared values and agreement create social order.

questions.q: Which is a key ethical issue researchers must consider?
options: Gaining informed consent and protecting participants from harm
Making the study as expensive as possible
questions.explain: Ethical research requires informed consent, confidentiality and protecting participants from harm.

options: The results can be repeated to get the same findings
The data gives a true, authentic picture of what it claims to measure
questions.explain: Validity is about whether data is genuine and accurately reflects reality, giving a true picture.

options: The ruling class who own the means of production
questions.explain: The bourgeoisie are the capitalist ruling class who own the means of production and profit from workers' labour.

questions.q: Marxism is best described as a:
options: Conflict theory based on class division and inequality
Consensus theory based on shared values
questions.explain: Marxism is a conflict theory focusing on class division between owners and workers under capitalism.

questions.q: A 'structured interview' is one in which:
options: The conversation is free-flowing with no set questions
The interviewer asks the same set of pre-decided questions in a fixed order
No questions are asked at all
questions.explain: A structured interview uses a fixed set of standardised questions, making it more reliable but often less in-depth.

questions.q: The 'structure versus action' debate in sociology concerns whether:
options: Society shapes individuals or individuals shape society
Old theories are better than new ones
questions.explain: The structure-action debate asks whether social structures determine behaviour or whether individuals actively create society.

questions.q: A strength of postal/self-completion questionnaires is that they:
options: Always achieve a very high response rate
Can reach large numbers of people quickly and cheaply
questions.explain: Questionnaires can gather data from many people quickly and cheaply, though response rates and depth can be limited.

options: Reflects the wider population so findings can be generalised
Contains only volunteers who feel strongly
questions.explain: A representative sample mirrors the target population, allowing findings to be generalised to it.

options: Is always more reliable than primary data
Is collected first-hand by the researcher
Already exists, having been produced by others (e.g. official statistics, documents)
questions.explain: Secondary data already exists and was produced by others, such as official statistics or existing documents.

questions.q: Quantitative data is data in the form of:
questions.explain: Quantitative data is numerical, allowing measurement and statistical comparison.

questions.q: Which pairing of perspective and key idea is correct?
questions.explain: Feminism is correctly linked to patriarchy; the other pairings mismatch the perspective with the wrong concept.
